column1: # scripts/lib/verbs.tsv — the ONE source for every cckit verb (#555).
# Read by bin/cckit (help, `<verb> --help`, `commands`, the alias path), by scripts/lib/verbs.sh and
# by scripts/verbs-check.sh, which fails on drift between this file and the dispatcher's case labels,
# the CLI reference page, skills/routing.yaml and scripts/forge-report.sh.
# Format: tab-separated, one row per line, exactly 10 fields; `#` lines and blank lines are skipped.
#   2 kind      group   a heading of `cckit help`; name = group id, question = the heading
#               verb    a top-level verb; the count of these rows is the ratchet in
#               default what bare `cckit` runs; never typed
#               alias   an old name; the dispatcher prints a one-line notice and runs <target>
#   3 target    alias: the verb it runs · every other kind: -
#   4 group     the group id the verb is listed under in `cckit help` (- for group and alias rows)
#   5 needs     git   runs on git alone
#               forge reads or writes the forge (GitHub) when one is configured
#   6 skill     the skill under skills/ that drives the verb, or -
#   7 ownhelp   yes: after the entry, `cckit <verb> --help` also prints the verb's own help
#   8 question  the question the verb answers, in the reader's words
#   9 prompt    one prompt to paste into an agent; never an issue number (rules/authoring.md § 2)
#  10 usage     the usage lines; a literal \n separates lines
# Rows are listed in the order `cckit help` prints them: each group, then its verbs.
